interface.block_wall_rule.value: at every step of a stretch (each block, from its first step to the step at which it ends; the start hold with the check-out; each gap between blocks; the time after the last block), the wall-clock time of the stretch's step replies so far may not exceed the stretch's world time so far plus 5 s; a call that would exceed it is cut there: in a block it is a protocol error and the block ends, outside a block the controller's process is ended and started again (interface.restart) and no job is lost

interface.class.value: Controller with setup(session), plan(job, frame), step(frame)

interface.command_fields.unit: field names of a step reply
value: event: the string "none", "done" or "ready" (left out: "none"; any other value, null included, is a malformed reply)

interface.event_rule.value: the event done or ready is accepted only when all five conditions hold, checked in this order: it is in an applied reply (on time, well formed, with a command); its frame is one of the job being flown; no event was accepted for this job before; it is of the job's kind (done for a leg or slew, ready for a view); its frame's time is at or after the time of the last setpoint of the job's accepted plan. An ignored event is named with its reason (step_not_applied, no_job, already_accepted, wrong_kind, before_last_setpoint) in the next frame's notices.

interface.frame_fields.unit: field names of a step frame; no estimate, no supervisor timer

interface.frame_notices.unit: one more field of every frame the controller receives (plan and step): what the runner says about the controller's last replies

entry_forms.event_ignored: {kind: event_ignored, job_id or null, event: done | ready, t: the frame's time, reason: step_not_applied | no_job | already_accepted | wrong_kind | before_last_setpoint}
entry_forms.plan: {kind: plan, job_id, valid: true} or {kind: plan, job_id, valid: false, rule: plan.max_setpoints | plan.limit_rule | plan.consistency | plan.start_tolerance | plan.end_tolerance | interface.plan_cpu_s | interface.plan_wall_s, setpoint: index or null}
entry_forms.protocol_error: {kind: protocol_error, call: plan | step, what: text}

value.where: a list in every frame the controller receives (plan and step), empty in most; a notice is given once, in the first frame sent after its cause

interface.late_reply.value: a step that uses more than its processor budget is not applied: the previous command stays, and the next n step calls are skipped, n = overrun divided by the step budget, rounded up (counted in step calls, not in world time)

interface.on_time_share_gate.unit: share of steps answered inside the processor budget, over the whole run

value.plan (processor or wall): the job is treated as one with an invalid plan: it scores 0 and the block goes on; the controller's process is ended only when the cap was reached while the runner waited for the reply
value.setup (processor or wall): every start of the session (the first and each restart) draws on one allowance of interface.setup_cpu_s and interface.setup_wall_s summed over the starts; a start that would use more than what is left is cut there, and a restart that is needed when nothing is left is not made: a set-up overrun, that session scores 0; the other sessions are flown
value.setup failure: a start that cannot go on (the import of controller.py or Controller() raises, the process ends at its start) or a setup that raises or replies malformed: a set-up failure, that session scores 0; the other sessions are flown
value.step, processor: the reply is not applied, the previous command stays, and the next n step calls are skipped, n = overrun divided by the step budget, rounded up
value.step, wall (the running bound of its str: in a block the block ends, as for a protocol error; outside a block the process is ended and started again (interface.block_wall_rule); in the check-out the rest of the check-out goes to the built-in controller

interface.plan_cpu_s.unit: s of processor time per job

value: accept with a list of setpoints, each a list [t, position, velocity, acceleration, attitude, body rate, angular acceleration]: t a number (s), attitude a list of 4 numbers (x, y, z, w), every other entry a list of 3 numbers
refuse with one reason of refusal.reasons

interface.plan_wall_s.unit: s of wall clock per job

interface.restart.value: The controller's process is started once per session. When it has ended (it exited, or the runner ended it because its reply stream could not go on: a reply line over interface.reply_line_cap_bytes, the stream closed, a line the client did not write, a call cut at its wall allowance or at a processor cap reached while waiting) it is started again before the next call, fresh: Controller() and setup(session) again with the same session paper, nothing of its earlier state handed to it. Every start of a session (the first and each restart) draws on the session's one set-up allowance, interface.setup_cpu_s of processor time and interface.setup_wall_s of wall clock summed over the starts (the interpreter's start, the import of controller.py, Controller() and setup all count); when it is used up: a set-up overrun (interface.overrun), that session scores 0 and no further start is made. The mass profile of the first setup stands; a later setup reply is checked for its form only.

interface.setup_cpu_s.unit: s of processor time per session

interface.setup_reply.value: nothing, or a mass profile (mass, centre of mass, inertia) to be sent to the robot before the first block

interface.setup_wall_s.unit: s of wall clock per session

interface.step_cpu_ms.unit: ms of processor time per step

interface.step_period_ms.unit: ms between two step calls (62.5 Hz), constant

interface.watchdog_s.unit: s without an applied command before the propulsion stops

jobs.block_budget.value: B = S + sum over every job announced for the block of (k x t_j + F_j). t_j = max(trap(d_j, a, v), trap(theta_j, alpha, omega)) with trap(x, A, V) = 2 sqrt(x / A) if x <= V^2 / A, else x / V + V / A; d_j and theta_j are the distance and the turn angle between the body pose that meets the goal of the job before (here the last job before it in the block's list that is not a hold, whether it is a request or not; the block's start pose if there is none) and the body pose that meets this job's goal; v, a, omega, alpha are the four hard limits of the job's mode (a job that names a mode that is not in the session paper's list of modes takes the block's mode); a hold has t_j = 0. F_j = 2.5 s for a leg or slew (its end window), the duration for a hold, 1.7 s for a view (its capture). S = jobs.spin_up_term for a block that starts with a mode change, else 0. k = jobs.budget_factor.

jobs.block_clock.value: the block's clock starts at the first step of the block (for block 3 the mode command is issued at that instant), runs in world time and stops for nothing; plan calls take no world time; when it reaches B the block ends and the built-in controller takes over

jobs.camera_mount_m.unit: m, optical centre of the imaging camera in body axes

jobs.capture_s.unit: s the imaging camera needs for one picture after the event ready

jobs.finished.value: a job is finished if its fixed window (end window, hold, capture) has closed when the block's clock reaches B; a job that is not finished or not started then scores 0 and, if it counts toward the score, stays in the mean; a refused request takes no time

jobs.spin_up_term.value: S = |n_new - n_old| / 200 + 2.0 s with n = 2000, 2500, 2800 rpm for fan levels 1, 2, 3 (4.5 s into the quiet mode, 3.5 s into the precision mode)

mode.fan_level.unit: fan level of each mode in the releases of the acceptance sessions (nominal was 3 before 2020-10-23)

plan.acceleration_limit.unit: hard limits of the mode's block in the flight-mode file of the release in force, undivided

plan.check_order.value: plan.max_setpoints, plan.limit_rule, plan.consistency (the times, then the forward integration), plan.start_tolerance, plan.end_tolerance (the rates, then a leg's or slew's last pose); the first broken one is named with its setpoint index; a plan's attitudes are normalised before the check and an attitude of norm zero is a malformed reply

plan.consistency.value: setpoint times increase strictly and are at most 1.0 s apart; a setpoint integrated forward at its constant acceleration to the time of the next one agrees with it within 2 mm and 0.2 degrees in pose and 2 mm/s and 0.2 deg/s in velocity and body rate

plan.end_tolerance.unit: last setpoint against the job's goal

value.every kind: the last setpoint has zero velocity, acceleration, body rate and angular acceleration
value.view: the pose of the last setpoint is not checked

plan.limit_rule.value: every setpoint of a plan: the norms of velocity, acceleration, body rate and angular acceleration are at most the four hard limits of the job's mode (plan.speed_limit, plan.acceleration_limit), relative tolerance 1e-6; checked when plan returns, before the job starts; a plan that breaks it is invalid

plan.start_tolerance.unit: first setpoint against the body pose that meets the goal of the job before (the block's start pose for the first job)

safety.protocol_error.value: a malformed or non-finite reply ends the block

score.end_window_s.unit: s after done over which the true end errors are averaged; the controller keeps holding

controller_account.why: the account the controller's process runs under when the runner runs as root (its group, no supplementary groups); read only then

budget_match_s.why: a block budget on the paper against the runner's own computation

gap_eps_s.why: floating-point slack of the largest setpoint gap

time_eps_s.why: floating-point slack of time comparisons (an event at or after the last setpoint's time; the block clock)

what: the runner's configuration: every number from the task's table by key (value and unit), and the numbers stated in the table's rule texts read out by key
